chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Zurarah said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I do not like for a Muslim man to marry a co-wife who was his mother's rival (had been married to his father alongside his mother) with someone other than his father.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ضَرَّة: Co-wife or rival wife (specifically one sharing a husband with another woman)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman who was previously married to one's father alongside one's mother?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) expresses his dislike for a Muslim man to marry a woman who previously served as a co-wife to his mother during her husband's lifetime, specifically if she was married to someone other than the man's father. This ruling highlights the social and familial nuances of polygyny and the status of the mother's rivals, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining familial dignity and avoiding close kinship ties that may lead to domestic discord.
